text: Πρὸς Πέτρον Ἰλλούστριον. Nomen dignitatis est. Basil. Eccl. 7 : Οἱ ἀπὸ πατρικίων ἕως ἰλλουστρίων εἰσὶν οἱ συγκλητικοί. Justin. Novella 13 : Ἡμεῖς γὰρ οὐδενὶ τὴν εἰρημένην ἀρχὴν παραδώσομεν πλὴν εἰ μὴ τῶν μεγαλοπρεπεστάτων ἰλλουστρίων. Erat igitur Petrus hic τῶν ἐν ἀρχῇ, homo senatorii ordinis; nempe εὐγενής, ut Glossæ Basilic. Vir nobilis, et quod præcipuum, spectatæ fidei et probæ orthodoxus, cujus alia nescimus, quam quæ Maximus una et altera epist. de illo insinuavit.
anchorLine: Τοῦ αὐτοῦ πρὸς Πέτρον Ἰλλούστριον (a)
en: To Peter Illustrius. The name of a dignity. Basil. Eccl. 7: those from the patricians up to the illustrii are the senators. Justinian, Novella 13: for we shall hand over the said office to no one except one of the most magnificent illustrii. So this Peter was one of those in office, a man of senatorial rank, that is well-born, as the Basilic Gloss has it. A nobleman and, above all, of approved faith and sound orthodoxy; we know nothing else of him than what Maximus has hinted in one or two letters.
